question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-6{t}^{3}+6t+12)+{x}_{2}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-3t-2)+{x}_{3}(-3{t}^{2}+2t) & =-9{t}^{3}+19t+18 \\ (-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}){t}^{3}+(-2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+(6{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3})t+(12{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}) & =-9{t}^{3}+19t+18.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=19 \\ 12{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=18.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 2 & 19 \\ 12 & -2 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 5{x}_{3}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-2{x}_{2}-3\cdot 2=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-3.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
-6{x}_{1}+(-3)=-9\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{2}=-3.$
